chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

My father used to perform Sa'ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, covering the distance from the door of Ibn Abbad until he raised his feet from the ravine, not reaching the alleyway of the progeny of Abu Husayn.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the two hills between which pilgrims walk during Hajj and Umrah.
key_terms.الْمَرْوَة: Al-Marwa, the second hill in the Sa'ee ritual.
key_terms.الْمَسِيل: The ravine or valley floor between the two hills.
key_terms.يَسْعَى: To perform Sa'ee, the ritual walking between Safa and Marwa.

ai.seo_question: What was the specific extent of Imam al-Sadiq's Sa'ee between Safa and Marwa?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the specific juristic practice (fiqh) of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the boundaries of the Sa'ee, noting he walked from the door of Ibn Abbad to the stream (Masil) rather than the entire valley. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the Sa'ee is confined to the area between the two hills as defined by the Prophet's practice, distinguishing it from the Hanafi view of the entire valley. It underscores the importance of following the Imams' precise ritual implementations in Hajj and Umrah.
